Pharmaceutical Sciences

Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam

← Back to search
About this programme

UCR currently cannot construct a sufficiently close programme for a meaningful curriculum comparison.

VU Pharmaceutical Sciences studies the early stages of drug discovery through molecular biology and chemistry. Students learn to identify drug targets, design and synthesise compounds, test their activity and safety, and conduct pharmaceutical research.

UCR offers relevant study in pharmacology, biochemistry, molecular-cell biology and biomedical laboratory methods. Its Pharmacology course includes drug targets and quantitative pharmacokinetics. These contributions do not form a complete programme centred on medicinal chemistry, synthesis, compound testing and pharmaceutical molecular modelling. We therefore show the verified VU curriculum without presenting a UCR programme as a comparable alternative.

Academic year: 2026–2027

External pathway: General bachelor; no formal graduation specialisation

The 180 EC pathway includes 60 EC in each of the first two years, 12 EC of compulsory third-year courses, an 18 EC individual pharmaceutical project and 30 EC of open study. Chemistry- or biology-focused minors are optional. Project entry requires all first-year courses, the specified practicals including modelling and 120 EC. Laboratory safety, language and tutorial requirements add no credits.
